text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Constitutional Council likely to endorse the Thursday parliamentary election result on Monday.
- With new parliament dominated by conservatives and Islamists, pro-democratic political forces face the risk of being sidelined.
- Amadou Toumani Toure, head of the 70-strong Organisation of African Unity (OAU) poll watchers, says the election took place in good conditions.
- Kamel Said, Arab league deputy chief, says the Algerian election is a milestone to restore a state of law.
- Former ruling National Liberation Front (FLN) has scored well in the general election surprising many observers who believed the FLN was dead.

- National Democratic Rally, grouping President Liamine Zeroual's supporters, has to forge alliances with other parties after the poll gave the Rally first position in parliament but left it far from an overall majority.
- Arab and African observers say they were very satisfied with Algeria's general election.
